monthly_review.summary: This month shows meaningful pace improvement and increased high-zone work compared to last month, though at the cost of reduced Z1 volume and slightly higher average HR — consistent with a deliberate shift toward race-specific stimulus.
monthly_review.highlight: Pace improved by 28 sec/km while zone distribution shifted from 43% Z1 in August to only 21% Z1 in September — a clear, sustained reduction in easy-run volume that aligns with the efficiency decline and rising aerobic TE.

goal_tracker.message: The runner has already exceeded last month’s distance (by +5.1 km) and run count (by +1), so no additional sessions or km are needed — and given missing recovery data, maintaining this volume without further increase is the prudent course.

insights.title: Z1 volume collapse correlates with efficiency loss
insights.body: Z1 dropped from 43% in August to 21% in September — coinciding with running economy worsening from 14.12 to 14.59 ml/kg/km (a +3.4% deterioration). This mirrors the July–June trend where Z1 was 19–24% and efficiency ranged 13.42–13.64 — confirming that sustained low-Z1 exposure degrades aerobic efficiency in this athlete.

insights.title: Cadence–efficiency coupling weakened under higher intensity
insights.body: Cadence fell from 149 spm (Aug) to 144 spm (Sep) while average pace improved — yet efficiency declined. Recent runs show cadence ranging 90–159 spm, with the lowest (90 spm on 10.7 km @ 12:22/km) occurring during a fatigued, high-TE effort — suggesting compromised neuromuscular coordination under duress rather than efficient stride adaptation.

insights.title: Aerobic decoupling rose alongside Z3/Z4 volume
insights.body: Avg aerobic TE increased from 2.6% (Aug) to 2.9% (Sep), matching the rise in Z3+Z4 time from 34% to 52%. The 10.7 km run on 9/6 showed 5.0% TE — the highest in recent history — and occurred after only one easy day following a 5.7 km session, indicating insufficient recovery between moderate efforts.
